A nice long read trip foray into the US. Mostly unplanned, and with at least 3 friends. It's more about the adventure of the journey than the destination.

For me, it was a trip through Southern Colorado visiting Great Sand Dune National Park, Mesa Verde National Park, and riding the Durango to Silverton Train. We camped for the whole week and had some fantastic coffee in Mancos. Listened to Jason Mraz's Beautiful Mess album just about the whole way. What a great trip.
A trip to my porch with a beer and a good book,

Annual week long trip to Lake Anna, Virginia.

Usually about a dozen of us rent a house with a private dock and boathouse. A ton of yard space, a boat, jet skis, wakeboarding, tubing, fishing, cow tipping, corn hole, smash bros, movies, group meals, just doing you.. Did I mention... it's all free.

Last year I drove to NYC from Tucson. Saw a lot of corn and mullets in the Midwest. Got sick from White Castle burgers in Jersey, then got called a bozo by some old guy in Queens. I got the flavors of America, and it was cool.

Visiting family in Nova Scotia. Done it twice, 22~ hour drive one-way.

First time was when I was a kid, second time was last year. I'll never forget it.

I would have to say... the summer of 2011..

I took a cruise down the Caribbean with my folks and had an absolute blast, went jet skiing, diving with all sorts of exotic fish, went to the Bacardi rum distillery, went on some awesome tours and met some great people.

We were on the explorer of the seas, a ship owned and operated by Royal Caribbean International. If you ever decide to take a cruise, I would definitely recommend going with Royal Caribbean. They may be a little more pricey, but the food, and staff on board go that extra mile to make sure you're happy and will do everything they can if you're not.

Our ship was being followed by a tropical storm for most of our cruise, so there were a few days and nights where it was a bit rough on the water, but I wouldn't have it any other way. I definitely have my sea legs. Some of the other passengers, however, were not so fortunate.
Where I'm from, we call it Balconville, which is French for balcony (or porch) city. Essentially, my favorite vacation is a staycation.
Road trip from a beach of South Carolina to San Francisco, then up through the redwoods and back down State Route 1. Flew back, but it was a great trip.
My couch and no phone calls from work....I can dream.

A few years back I went to Yellowstone in South Dakota. It was absolutely beautiful, though the buffalo take it upon themselves to set up traffic blocks, and sometimes it takes a while for them to move. The Badlands were even better. I'd highly recommend going to anyone who lives in the US (and everywhere else if you visit the country).
